displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The most economical historical model is a minimally biographical Jewish teacher whose remembered law and kingdom activity was rapidly transformed through revelation, communal conflict, and literary mimesis.

novelty.explanation: This steelman makes the historical claim deliberately minimal and integrates the participant’s separate literary and social-development arguments.

premises.text: Paul’s occasional correspondence lowers the expected quantity of biography, while named meetings with Cephas and James provide a plausible interpersonal bridge to an earlier movement.

novelty.explanation: It develops the genre argument while treating personal contact only as a plausible channel rather than demonstrated information transfer.

premises.text: A reconstructed early Jewish teaching complex concerning law, mission, and kingdom is more naturally situated within disputes among Jewish communities than within a fully formed celestial-savior biography.

novelty.explanation: It narrows the Q claim and avoids treating literary comparison with historical figures as direct proof of historicity.

premises.text: Josephus becomes meaningful cumulative evidence if authentic kinship wording, ordinary authorial usage, and contextual identification converge, even though no component should carry the case alone.

novelty.explanation: It answers the strongest textual objection by framing Josephus as convergent and defeasible rather than automatically decisive evidence.

premises.text: Extensive Markan mimesis is compatible with historical transformation when residual teaching, social location, and interpersonal continuity jointly require fewer independent inventions than complete reification.

novelty.explanation: It supplies the comparative criterion missing from the participant’s appeal to mortal epic models.

conclusion.text: Taken cumulatively, these considerations modestly favor a historical Jewish nucleus later mythologized, without requiring confidence in detailed Gospel biography or denying extensive literary construction.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion combines the main historicist lines while limiting the result to a minimal historical nucleus.

newArguments.title: Distributed convergence test
newArguments.text: Instead of demanding that any single source independently prove Jesus, compare whether several differently situated traces converge on the same minimal social profile: a Jewish figure, associates, law controversy, execution, and subsequent resurrection belief. Dependence can explain shared wording, but it becomes progressively less economical when it must separately generate kinship, interpersonal networks, and Jewish legal location across distinct genres. This is a cumulative argument only; each proposed trace still requires individual authentication and dependency analysis.

novelty.explanation: This newly introduces a formal cumulative-convergence test rather than extending any single transcript argument.

newArguments.title: Transformation-cost comparison
newArguments.text: Compare the editorial cost of two models across successive layers. A historical-nucleus model predicts selective preservation, theological reinterpretation, and expanding narrative detail around an initially sparse person. A reification model predicts coordinated conversion of revelations, scripture, and communal teachings into a recent teacher with relatives, associates, disputes, and execution. The better explanation is whichever requires fewer independent auxiliary assumptions across Paul, teaching traditions, Mark, and Josephus, not whichever can merely accommodate each item after the fact.

novelty.explanation: This is a new comparative model-selection framework based on auxiliary assumptions across the entire evidentiary sequence.

thesis.text: The earliest recoverable evidence is compatible with a revelatory Christ, while earthly biography emerges through literary reification and disputed later identification rather than securely independent memory.

novelty.explanation: This steelman replaces categorical source denial with the more defensible claim of comparative compatibility and insecure independence.

premises.text: Paul’s revelatory emphasis and sparse earthly placement create a likelihood question that cannot be dismissed solely by labeling his letters occasional.

novelty.explanation: It strengthens the Pauline argument by demanding explicit expectations under both models rather than relying on silence alone.

premises.text: Jewish law, kingdom, and mission content can arise through scripture, revelation, and community formation, so such content does not uniquely identify an originating earthly teacher.

novelty.explanation: It combines the strongest non-uniqueness replies into one bounded source-generation premise.

premises.text: Markan and Matthean literary construction can transform prior theological material into earthly scenes; direct dependence should be argued through patterns rather than asserted categorically.

novelty.explanation: It preserves literary reification while correcting the under-supported claim of comprehensive Pauline conversion.

premises.text: Josephus cannot securely anchor the historical model unless wording, intended referent, kinship sense, and transmission survive plausible cultic and ben Damneus alternatives.

novelty.explanation: It develops the Josephian challenge as a sequence of necessary identification checks.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, a revelatory-origin model remains a serious comparative explanation, especially where alleged historical anchors depend upon contested reconstruction, dependency, or textual identification.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately combines the principal con lines without claiming that possibility alone proves mythicism.

newArguments.title: Expected-reference matrix
newArguments.text: Construct an explicit matrix of contexts in which Paul discusses apostleship, lineage, law, crucifixion, teaching, and resurrection. For each context, preregister which earthly details should be expected under a recent-teacher model and which revelatory or scriptural references should be expected under a celestial-origin model. This converts a loose argument from silence into comparative likelihood evidence and prevents selective attention to whichever omissions appear surprising after reading the letters.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new preregistered likelihood method for evaluating Pauline omissions and references symmetrically.

newArguments.title: Independent-anchor audit
newArguments.text: Treat every proposed historical anchor as a chain whose strength cannot exceed its weakest necessary link: date, authenticity, independence, referent, and semantic interpretation. Apply this audit separately to Q, Papias, Johannine witness rhetoric, Josephus, and Acts reception. Correlations among sources should count cumulatively only after shared dependence has been excluded. The method does not presume mythicism; it explains why several individually uncertain anchors may fail to produce strong combined evidence.

novelty.explanation: This newly introduces a weakest-link audit for determining when uncertain sources may legitimately accumulate.
